title: Custom init in an Extension

docs.title: Initialization — Memberwise Initializers for Structure Types

hints: Writing an `init` inside a struct removes the free memberwise initialiser.
Put your custom `init(name:)` in an **extension** so both initialisers exist.
`extension Player { init(name: String) { self.name = name; self.number = name.unicodeScalars.reduce(0) { $0 + Int($1.value) } % 100 } }`.
jsBridge: Structs get a free memberwise `init`, like a TS class with parameter properties. Writing a custom `init` inside the struct **removes** it, while writing it in an **extension** keeps both. There's no JS parallel.

compass.q: TS `constructor(public name: string)` gives a free constructor. Why does Swift drop the memberwise init when you add your own?
Is the memberwise init `public` for a public struct? (No, it's `internal`.) Why does that matter for packages?
Custom init in an extension vs a static factory (`Player.named("x")`): which reads better?
Previews and tests often need convenience inits. Where do you put them (`#if DEBUG` extensions)?
